findings_resolved: FINDING-02 (partial): Decoupled EncryptionService from Microsoft.AspNetCore.Cryptography.KeyDerivation by migrating to standard BCL System.Security.Cryptography.Rfc2898DeriveBytes.Pbkdf2.

FINDING-06: Introduced FileStorageSettings.CanonicalizePath and LocalFileStorageSettings automatic canonicalization to resolve relative paths against a safe application data root (LocalApplicationData/MelloSilveiraTools or STORAGE_BASE_DIRECTORY) instead of System32 or '/'.

FINDING-07: Implemented strict path traversal validation against '..', path separators ('/', '\'), control/dangerous characters, and Windows reserved device names in identifier, context, and fileName. Verified path containment within BaseDirectory via Path.GetRelativePath and prefix checks.

FINDING-08: Configured EnumerationOptions with MatchCasing = MatchCasing.CaseInsensitive in LocalFileStorageService (for file/directory enumerations and case-insensitive directory segment resolution) and in PluginFileProcessor, ensuring full compatibility with Linux case-sensitive filesystems (ext4).
FINDING-14: Standardized LocalFileStorageService metadata extraction to use LastWriteTimeUtc instead of CreationTimeUtc to avoid unreliable birth time behavior in Linux POSIX environments.
data_payload.changelog_entry:
### Security & Cross-Platform Portability (Storage & Encryption)
- Replaced `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Cryptography.KeyDerivation.KeyDerivation.Pbkdf2` in `EncryptionService.cs` with BCL standard `System.Security.Cryptography.Rfc2898DeriveBytes.Pbkdf2`, eliminating ASP.NET Core runtime dependency in core encryption [FINDING-02].
- Hardened `LocalFileStorageService.cs` against path traversal attacks by introducing strict validation against traversal segments (`..`), path separators (`/`, `\\`), control/dangerous characters, and reserved device names across identifier, context, and file names [FINDING-07].
- Added `FileStorageSettings.CanonicalizePath` and automatic canonicalization in `LocalFileStorageSettings.cs` to resolve relative paths against a secure application directory rather than working directories like System32 or '/' [FINDING-06].
- Configured `EnumerationOptions` with `MatchCasing.CaseInsensitive` in `LocalFileStorageService.cs` and `PluginFileProcessor.cs`, preventing filesystem casing collisions on Linux ext4 [FINDING-08].
- Adopted `LastWriteTimeUtc` instead of `CreationTimeUtc` in `LocalFileStorageService.cs` for reliable cross-platform POSIX file metadata [FINDING-14].

output_summary: Implemented security and cross-platform portability remediations across Core and Plugins: migrated PBKDF2 to standard BCL API, added strict path traversal and device name safeguards, canonicalized relative storage paths, enabled case-insensitive filesystem enumeration, and adopted LastWriteTimeUtc metadata timestamps.
justification_for_decisions: 1. BCL PBKDF2: Utilizing Rfc2898DeriveBytes.Pbkdf2 eliminates runtime reliance on Microsoft.AspNetCore.Cryptography.KeyDerivation, ensuring Core can run in lean container and console environments without ASP.NET Core runtime. 2. Path Traversal & Device Name Validation: Proactive validation of identifier, context, and fileName before IO operations prevents directory traversal (../, ..\\) and reserved device name collisions on Windows/Linux. 3. Safe Path Canonicalization: Relative storage paths resolve to Environment.SpecialFolder.LocalApplicationData or STORAGE_BASE_DIRECTORY to prevent service daemons from writing to System32 or filesystem root. 4. Case-Insensitive Matching: Linux ext4 filesystems treat casing strictly; using EnumerationOptions.MatchCasing = CaseInsensitive ensures directory and file resolution matches existing entities regardless of input casing variations. 5. LastWriteTimeUtc: Statx creation times are unreliable or zeroed in Linux containers/overlayfs, whereas LastWriteTimeUtc is universally supported.
